reference: Oqtepa Lavash bot screenshots supplied by the product owner
principles: Use a command menu and a small persistent reply keyboard for navigation.
Require location confirmation before creating a delivery order.
Keep full product details separate from compact category buttons.
Authorize staff Telegram actions by employee and branch, not only group chat id.
Treat payment providers and Mini App as separate rollout decisions.

phases.name: Navigation, commands, and access control
work: Register customer commands: start, menu, cart, orders, profile, branches, support, cancel.
Configure Telegram Menu Button to open the command list.
Add a persistent reply keyboard for menu, cart, orders, profile, branches, and support.
Use contextual Back and Home controls only inside checkout steps.
Verify staff callback users against employee roles and branch access.
acceptance: Typing slash shows the command list.
The Menu control appears beside the text field.
A non-authorized group member cannot change an order status.
Every navigation action has a predictable destination.

phases.name: Delivery location and address confirmation
work: Request current Telegram location or allow a saved/manual address.
Validate the service zone before checkout continues.
Reverse-geocode the selected point through a configured provider with manual fallback.
Collect house, apartment, entrance, floor, and landmark.
Show map link and formatted address with Confirm, Edit, and Change location actions.
Persist confirmed coordinates in the order and optionally in the saved-address book.
acceptance: Delivery order cannot be created without confirmed location and address details.
Outside-zone points receive a clear refusal.
Courier receives both readable address and coordinates.

phases.name: Catalog and basket experience
work: Use category-aware short labels in two-column product grids.
Remove repeated category words such as Lavash and Burger from buttons.
Move to one column when labels cannot fit safely.
Add catalog pagination, search, product photos, and product details.
Add order history detail, repeat order, and clear basket confirmation.
Add promo-code flow after business rules are defined.
acceptance: No product button truncates an important product distinction.
Category browsing works with large catalogs.
Basket total, delivery fee, and changes remain consistent.

phases.name: Payments, support, and retention
work: Offer cash, Click, and Payme according to active branch settings.
Integrate Telegram invoice only after a compatible provider is approved.
Add support routing, opening hours, and a human handoff policy.
Add order status notifications, re-order, favorites, bonus view, and targeted promotions.
acceptance: Payment state matches the backend order state.
Support requests reach the responsible team without exposing customer data.
Promotional messages use opt-in and rate limits.

phases.name: Operations and observability
work: Expose webhook health, pending updates, command/menu configuration, and dead-letter count in admin.
Add alerts for failed Telegram delivery and persistent webhook errors.
Track funnel metrics from start through paid/accepted order.
acceptance: Operations team can see a broken webhook before orders are missed.
Failed messages can be retried safely.
Dashboard separates customer and staff bot health.

phases.name: Optional Telegram Mini App
phases.decision: Build only if the native bot catalog becomes too dense. Native commands and checkout remain the fallback.
work: Open customer web menu inside Telegram
Validate init data server-side
Share basket and address state with the bot
